name: Re-belle
_comment_group: One more show under the Snapchat heading, cut to Hall of Femme's
design. Everything that makes it a Snapchat pack is Hall of Femme's
and comes from the same two presets rather than being restated here:
the frame fetch, the 540x960 vertical output, the transcription, the
rewrite that turns speech into report, the stated 40px, the twenty
characters to a line, the freeform text box, the drag.
What makes it this show rather than that one is three decisions, and
they are the three that were asked for: it is set in a signature
hand with picked words in Syne Bold, it is one colour throughout,
and it has no card. Each is argued where it is stated, and the last
two are the ones that reach further than they look - a caption on
the photograph instead of on a slab changes what has to hold it
legible, and a show with one colour has no palette to hand over.
The id is kebab-case ASCII because it is also the folder name and the
key everything else refers to; the name is the brand.
_comment_capture: The frame fetch, whole, from content/presets/snapchat-capture.json:
the slider's range, the 540x960 output, the transcription, and the
rewrite that turns it from speech into report. This channel has

_comment_title: Where this show parts company with the pack it was cut from. Hall of
Femme sets its captions in Telegraf - a 200-weight hairline for the
block, the 800 for a picked word - on a hot pink card, in sixteen
pairings the user chooses between. This one is set in Brittany
Signature, a joined signature hand, with picked words in Syne Bold,
in one purple, on nothing at all.
Two of those three follow from each other. Dropping the card is what
takes the caption off a ground somebody chose and puts it on forty
photographs nobody chose the contrast of, which is why `shadow`
comes back below and why `uppercase` and the highlight are worth
reading as decisions about legibility rather than about style.
The third is the face, and it is what the other two are in service

_comment_uppercase: Off, and this pack is the second under the Snapchat heading where
it is - Killer Bites is the other, and its note is worth reading
beside this one because the reasons are different.
The preset's argument for capitals is that at 40px with twenty
characters to a line a caption is three short beats rather than a
paragraph, and beats are what capitals are for. That argument is
about grotesques. This face is a signature hand, and a signature
hand has no capitals in the sense the preset means: its letters
are drawn to JOIN, and the joins live in the lower case. Set in
capitals it comes apart into twenty unconnected swash initials -
not a louder version of the same hand but a different and much
harder-to-read object, and the one thing that made it worth
choosing is gone.
It is applied at the draw and not to what is stored, so turning
it off changes only what the canvas does: the text box held the
user's own casing all along, and the highlight buttons already
offered the words as the canvas would set them (see the `cased`
note in js/text.js and editor.renderWordButtons).
It reaches the picked words too - `uppercase` is the block's and
there is one of it - so Syne Bold is set in lower case as well.
That is the right answer for the same reason at one remove: what
separates a picked word here is that it is suddenly a typeface
instead of a hand, and it does not need a second difference
stacked on top of it.

_comment_colors: Absent, deliberately, and worth the note because the pack this
one was cut from is the pack that INTRODUCED the feature, and the
next person to copy this folder will wonder where it went.
Hall of Femme offers four colours for the letters and four for
the card, and the point there is the pairing: what that show is
set in is which of sixteen combinations the user picked, so the
choice is genuinely part of the look. This show has one colour
and no card. `colors.panel` could not be offered even if somebody
wanted it - a palette for a slab needs a slab (see the note on
`colors` in js/channels.js) - and `colors.text` with a single
entry in it would be a row containing one button that repaints
the caption the colour it already is.
So the purple is stated as the channel's own answer above and
nothing is handed over. If the show ever gains a second colour
this is two lines and the row appears with it; a palette is for a

_comment_shadow: Back, and this is the one place this pack contradicts a sentence
the preset writes. Every channel under this heading that keeps
its card sets `shadow` to null, on the argument that a drop
shadow is what keeps type legible over a photograph nobody chose
the contrast of and there is no photograph under those letters -
there is a solid card doing the job completely.
The argument is right, and it is exactly why dropping the card
means picking the shadow back up. There IS a photograph under
these letters, on all forty stills, and this is the thinnest face
on the heading set in a dark colour: #431C64 on a night scene, on
dark hair, on a shadow in the corner of a room is a caption
nobody can read at all.
The numbers are NOT the skeleton's, and that is the whole of what
is different here. Every other channel in this app shadows LIGHT
type, so it throws black down and to the right and the dark rim
is what the letters are found against. Black behind dark purple
adds dark to dark: on the frames where the caption is in trouble
it would be invisible in a slightly larger way. What separates
dark ink from a dark picture is light, so the shadow is white.
Centred rather than offset, which is the other consequence of
the colour being inverted. An offset shadow reads as a shadow -
a direction, a light source, something the letters are casting -
and white light falling three pixels down and to the right reads
as a printing misregistration instead. With no offset it is a
halo: the letters lifted off the picture on every side equally,
which is what they need when the picture could be anything.
0.9 and blur 12 rather than something softer and wider. This is a
hairline hand - the strokes are a pixel or two across at the
thinnest, and a faint wide glow behind a stroke that thin is a
smudge the stroke disappears into. It has to be nearly solid and
tight to the letterform to read as an edge rather than as fog.
_comment_highlight: A picked word is set in Syne Bold, in the same purple as the rest
of the block. This is Hall of Femme's highlight exactly - the
colour is stated and it is the block's, so the recolour draws
what its neighbours are drawn in and the FACE is the whole of the
difference - with the one change that the two faces here are not
two cuts of a family but two different kinds of writing.
Which is why it can stay a recolour with no card under it, where
Conspiracy Central had to become a box the moment it dropped its
own. That pack sets near-white Anton and picks words out of it in
near-black on yellow, because a recolour of two words in a block
of near-white would be two words in a slightly different white as
far as anyone scrolling is concerned. Nothing here is slightly
different: a bold grotesque in the middle of a signature hand is
the loudest change two words can make without changing colour,
and it makes it at a glance on a phone.
Colour mode and word scope are the preset's, and the argument for
picking out words rather than lines lives there: a caption's line
breaks are wherever the sentence ran out of width, so picking a
LINE out picks out a fragment rather than a thought.
The shadow is stated to the same numbers as the block's letters,
and it has to be. A picked word takes `highlight.shadow` and not
the block's (see runRows in js/text.js), and the skeleton's
answer there is a soft black halo - which on this channel would
put the one dark rim in the block behind the one word that is
supposed to be the easiest to read, and light every other word
from a different source. The card-bearing packs never notice
because their letters are on a slab; on the photograph it is two
light sources in one sentence.
_comment_panel: No card. The argument is in `_comment_title` above and the two
consequences are the `shadow` and the `colors` beside it.
Stated as null rather than left out, because it cannot be left
out: `use` merges the preset UNDER this pack (see `expand` in
js/channels.js), so the card's shape, padding, corners and shadow
arrive from snapchat-caption.json whatever this pack says about
them. Null is how a pack cut from that preset declines the one
part of it that is a whole shape rather than a number.

their titles are not on the photograph, and Conspiracy Central - the
other pack here with no card - says that even when the title IS on
the photograph the gradient is still the wrong tool, because it is a
SIDE gradient drawn for a landscape thumbnail with a headline beside
across the width of a vertical still, so darkening one half of forty
pictures would shade half of every line and leave the other half
There is a third reason here, and it is the decisive one: this type
is dark. A gradient that darkened the picture behind it would be
working against the halo rather than with it - see `shadow` above,
where what these letters need from the picture is light.
